title: Communication in families: a Gulf perspective
citation: Argyle, M. (2014). Benefits produced by supportive social relationships. In H. O. F. Veiel & U. Baumann (Eds.), The Meaning and Measurement of Social Support (pp. 13-32). Taylor & Francis.
content:
Communication in families: a Gulf perspective.

In many Gulf families, close family ties, respect for elders and a strong sense of responsibility towards relatives are deeply valued. These strengths can provide comfort, belonging and practical support during difficult times. At the same time, people may find it difficult to express emotions openly, disagree respectfully, or discuss sensitive topics because they worry about causing conflict or disappointing loved ones. Healthy communication does not mean abandoning cultural values. It means finding respectful ways to express needs, listen to one another and work through differences while maintaining those important family bonds.
